_comment: What a developer must do, per license, when a trigger happens. severity: notice | disclose | relicense | restriction. authority slugs from sources.json.

obligations.requirement: Include the MIT copyright notice and permission notice in all copies or substantial portions (a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES or bundled LICENSE file satisfies this).
Keep the ISC copyright notice and permission notice with all copies.
Reproduce the copyright notice, the conditions list and the disclaimer in the documentation or other materials of binary distributions.
Reproduce the notice, conditions and disclaimer; do not use the names of the copyright holder or contributors to endorse or promote derived products without permission.
All advertising materials mentioning features or use of the software must display the acknowledgement clause naming the original authors (the 'advertising clause').
Give recipients a copy of the Apache License 2.0 and, if the work ships a NOTICE file, include a readable copy of the attribution notices it contains.
Cause any modified files to carry prominent notices stating that you changed the files.
No permission to use the licensor's trade names, trademarks or product names except for describing the origin of the work.
Patent grant terminates for anyone who files a patent lawsuit alleging the work infringes a patent (defensive termination, section 3).
Modifications to MPL-covered files must be made available in source form under MPL 2.0 (file-level copyleft). Files you add under other licenses are unaffected.
Inform recipients that the executable contains MPL-covered code and how to obtain the source of those files (section 3.2).

Weak (file-level) copyleft: if you modify EPL-2.0 licensed source code and distribute that code or binaries built from it outside your company, you must make the source of the modified files available under EPL-2.0. No obligation if you don't distribute outside your company, and unmodified add-on modules that are not a Modified Work of the program are not covered.

Allow users to relink the application with a modified library: dynamic linking, or ship object files for static linking; ship the library source and the LGPL text; give prominent notice that the library is used.
Modifications to the library itself must be released under LGPL-2.1 (or GPL) with source.

For a Combined Work: prominent notice of LGPL use, ship the GPL/LGPL texts, and either dynamic linking with a suitable shared-library mechanism or the minimal corresponding source/object to relink (LGPLv3 section 4).
The entire work that includes or links the GPL code must be licensed GPL-2.0 and complete corresponding source must be offered to every recipient.
The entire combined work must be licensed GPL-3.0; provide complete corresponding source, including Installation Information for consumer devices (anti-tivoization, section 6).
No source obligation for merely running GPLv3 software on a server (SaaS loophole); only distribution triggers copyleft. Use AGPL if you want network use covered.
If users interact with a modified version over a network, you must offer them the complete corresponding source of that running version (section 13).
The combined work must be AGPL-3.0 with source offered to recipients.

Section 13 ("Offering the Program as a Service"): if you make the functionality of the program available to third parties as a service, you must make the Service Source Code — the whole stack needed to run an equivalent service, not just your changes to the program — available under SSPL. No obligation for internal or unmodified use.
Production use is prohibited except as allowed by the Additional Use Grant until the Change Date (at most four years), after which the Change License applies.
You may not provide the software to third parties as a hosted or managed service, circumvent license keys, or remove licensing notices.
'The Software shall be used for Good, not Evil.' A use restriction; the FSF classes the license as nonfree.
No conditions. Note: CC0 explicitly does not grant patent rights (clause 4a).
No conditions; public-domain dedication with permissive fallback.
No conditions; even the notice need not be kept.
The font may be bundled with software but may not be sold by itself; modified fonts may not use Reserved Font Names.
Give appropriate credit, link to the license, and indicate if changes were made. Intended for content, not code.
Adaptations must be distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (or a compatible license such as GPLv3).
No license means all rights reserved: you may not copy, modify or redistribute the code. npm's 'UNLICENSED' value means the same.
Altered source versions must be plainly marked as such and must not be misrepresented as the original.
Keep the Boost license notice in source distributions; binaries carry no notice requirement.
Distribute derivative works under EUPL-1.2 or one of the compatible licenses in the Appendix (GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0, MPL-2.0, EPL-1.0, LGPL, CeCILL, OSL, EUPL) with source available.
